controls.title: Integrity and confidentiality of processing
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the underlying processing was lawful, that the technical and organizational measures were appropriate to the risk, or that confidentiality of the data itself was preserved. The chain is the audit trail, not the security control.
controls.what_we_prove: Every processing event affecting in-scope personal data is hash-linked, signed, and timestamp-anchored, producing a tamper-evident record an auditor can verify offline. Any retroactive edit or omission is mathematically detectable.

controls.title: Accountability — controller must be able to demonstrate compliance with Art. 5(1)
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the demonstrated processing was itself Art. 5(1)-compliant. The chain is the demonstrability mechanism; whether what it demonstrates actually satisfies the principles (lawfulness, purpose limitation, data minimization, etc.) is the controller's substantive obligation.
controls.what_we_prove: Aleutian's chain provides the controller with cryptographic evidence of processing events — tamper-evident ordering, signed timestamps, and offline-verifiable integrity — that an authority, DPO, or auditor can use to demonstrate compliance with Art. 5(1) principles. The chain converts the controller's processing history into a substrate they can produce on demand.

controls.title: Security of processing — logging subset
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the security measures themselves were appropriate, that encryption was correctly applied, or that resilience requirements were met. The chain records the evidence of monitoring; it is not the monitoring system.
controls.what_we_prove: Security-relevant events the controller emits to the chain (access decisions, integrity checks, suspected breaches) are stored with tamper-evident ordering and signed timestamps.

controls_out_of_scope.reason: lawfulness of processing is a legal determination, not chain-evidenced

records of processing activities (RoPA) is a static document describing categories of processing — the chain may host supporting evidence for individual processing events but does not satisfy the Art.30 record-keeping obligation itself
valid consent is a policy/UX question; the chain logs consent events, not their validity
special-category data lawful-basis is a legal determination
notice and transparency obligations are document-level, not chain-evidenced
data subject rights are workflow obligations; specific request handling is covered under DSAR features, not as a GDPR control claim here
erasure is a workflow obligation; deletion-cert evidence is a separate audit primitive, not a GDPR control claim here
data protection by design and by default is an architectural posture, not chain-evidenced
processor contracts are document-level, not chain-evidenced
breach notification is a workflow obligation; specific notifications may be logged but the obligation is procedural
DPIA is a document-level assessment, not chain-evidenced
DPO appointment, position, and tasks are organizational, not chain-evidenced
international transfer mechanisms are legal/contractual, not chain-evidenced
